- 🔴 **The mechanism is a STALE ODDS SNAPSHOT, not a stale schedule: the card's own `odds_pulled_at` is `2026-09-01T11:13:07Z`, so the 18:41 card is built on a SEVEN-AND-A-HALF-HOUR-OLD props pull.** ✅ **The books themselves had dropped him by the next pull — `data/2026-09-01/props-pitcher/2003.json.gz` (`20:03:08Z`) contains no Arrighetti row at all, where `1113.json.gz` does.**

🔴 **CONTROL (b) IS NEW AND IT IS WORTH KEEPING, BECAUSE IT USES A SOURCE THE FETCH CANNOT TOUCH.** **The repo's stored pitcher logs were collected by different code, on a different machine, before the games were played.** ➡️ **A fabricated 8/26 line has to satisfy BOTH the season block and a pre-slate snapshot to survive, and none did.**

### 🔴 THE HITTER HALF WAS CONTROLLED THE SAME WAY — AND IT CAUGHT A REAL FABRICATION

**21 distinct hitters, `data/latest/hitters.json.gz` (pulled `2026-08-26T10:02:52Z`) summed plus the fetched 8/26 line, matched to independently-fetched season blocks.**

🔴 **AND THE CONTROL EARNED ITS KEEP: ON ONE HITTER THE FETCH RETURNED A FABRICATED ROW AND THE CONTROL REJECTED IT.** **Asked for the `2026-08-26` element AND the last element of Nathan Lukes' game log, the response returned TWO DIFFERENT OBJECTS while asserting they were identical** — `H2/AB4/TB2/RBI2` labelled as 8/26 (it is his 8/25 line) beside `H1/AB3/TB4/RBI3`. ✅ **The row was DISCARDED and re-pulled; the re-pull gives `H1 · AB3 · TB4 · RBI3`, which reconciles exactly and the discarded reading does not.** ⛔ **His row is a LOSS on either reading, so no tally moved — but the fabrication was real and it was caught by arithmetic rather than by suspicion.** ➡️ **This is pre-publish check 27 and ledger rule 40 doing the job they were written for, on a summarising fetch, exactly as `Grading mechanics` warns.**

### 🔴🔴 THE 4+IP SPLIT OF THE MATCHED-CLASS CHECK IS MATHEMATICALLY BIASED ON EVERY OUTS BET AT A THRESHOLD OF 12 OR HIGHER. THIS CARD QUOTED THE BIASED NUMBER AS THE HEADLINE.

`[derived 2026-08-22 — a proof, not a measurement]`

**STEP 4B reports the matched class two ways: ALL starts, and starts where the pitcher recorded `outs ≥ 12` ("4+IP"). The 4+IP split exists to strip out starts abandoned early for reasons unrelated to the bet.** 🔴 **On an OUTS UNDER it does not do that. It deletes winners and keeps every loser.**

**THE PROOF, for an under at threshold `T`:**
- **A WIN is `outs ≤ T`. A LOSS is `outs > T`.**
- **The filter keeps `outs ≥ 12`.**
- ➡️ **Whenever `T ≥ 12`, EVERY loss already satisfies `outs > T ≥ 12` and is therefore KEPT with certainty.**
- ➡️ **But the winners with `outs < 12` are ALL REMOVED.**
- ⛔ **The filter can only ever delete winners and never a single loss. The resulting rate is a STRICT LOWER BOUND on the true rate, guaranteed by arithmetic, on every slate, for every pitcher.**

**AND IT RUNS THE OTHER WAY ON AN OVER: for `T ≥ 12` every WIN (`outs > T`) survives the filter and only LOSERS are removed, so the 4+IP figure is biased HIGH.**

⚠️ **THE SEVERITY SCALES WITH HOW FAR `T` SITS ABOVE 12.** **At `u18.5` the winning region is 0–18 and the filter removes only the 0–11 slice — a modest bias, which is why the 8/21 Sale row read a healthy 90.5%.** 🔴 **At `u15.5` the winning region is 0–15 and the filter removes 0–11, a large share of it. That is where the distortion bites, and `u15.5` is the most common outs rung on the board.**

### 🔴 WHAT IT DID TO THIS CARD — TWO PLAYS WERE MISREPRESENTED TO SAM, AND BOTH WERE MISREPRESENTED AGAINST THE BET

| Play | Biased 4+IP figure — **quoted as the headline** | **Unbiased ALL figure — what should have been quoted** |
|---|---|---|
| **Jake Irvin u15.5 outs vs MIA** (row 9) | 🔴 **46.9% (23/49)** — delivered to Sam as *"under half"* | ✅ **55.2% (32/58)** |
| **Ryan Johnson u15.5 outs vs TEX** *(not carded — asked about in conversation)* | 🔴 **38.5% (20/52)** | ✅ **50.0% (32/64)** |

⚠️ 🔴 **THE FLAG ON IRVIN SURVIVES EITHER WAY — 55.2% is still well below his 70.9% blend, and the class still disagrees with the model's +17.4 edge.** ⛔ **But 46.9% and 55.2% are different claims, and the card led with the one that could not have been anything else.**

➡️ **CORRECTED PROCEDURE, EFFECTIVE NOW: on an OUTS bet at `T ≥ 12`, the ALL-STARTS figure is the headline and the 4+IP figure is reported only with the words "biased low on unders / high on overs by construction" attached.** ⛔ **On STRIKEOUT bets the filter is NOT provably biased in either direction — a short outing is a plausible loss for a K over and a plausible win for a K under — so 4+IP stays informative there and STEP 4B is unchanged for strikeouts.**

🆕 **PRE-REGISTERED AS T23 in `claude/owed-tests.md`: replace the `outs ≥ 12` filter on OUTS markets with a filter that cannot touch the outcome — candidates are (a) drop only starts ended by injury or ejection, and (b) no filter at all, reporting ALL starts alone. Single specification, decided at the September re-fit, before the data is touched again.** ⛔ **NOT adopted now; only the REPORTING order changes today, and no probability on this card was recomputed.**

🔴 **THIS WAS DERIVED, NOT MEASURED, AND THAT MAKES IT STRONGER, NOT WEAKER — it is a property of the filter, so it has been corrupting every outs-under class figure this project has ever printed, on every card, since STEP 4B was introduced.** ⚠️ **Prompted by Sam asking about a second `u15.5` outs play, which put two of them side by side and made the pattern visible.**

### 🔴🔴 THE MATCHED CLASS IS MATCHED ON THE WRONG AXIS FOR OUTS MARKETS. SAM CAUGHT IT. IT MOVED TWO PLAYS BY 10–17 POINTS.

`[measured 2026-08-22, point-in-time]` **Sam, on the Ryan Johnson u15.5 outs question:** *"look at pitchers of ryan johnsons caliber against texas… in all of those 64 texas games half of them may have gone over or under, but how many of those pitchers are tiers above ryan johnson, this is an important thing to catch for trying to snipe these types of pitchers for an under"*

🔴 **HE IS RIGHT, AND THE DEFECT IS STRUCTURAL. STEP 4B SELECTS COMPARABLES BY `±1.5 K/9` — A STRIKEOUT-RATE BAND. FOR AN OUTS BET THE RELEVANT AXIS IS NOT STRIKEOUT RATE, IT IS DURABILITY.** **A `±1.5 K/9` band cheerfully puts a workhorse ace next to a short-leash arm with a 6.41 ERA, because K/9 says almost nothing about how long a start lasts.**

**REBUILT ON TRAILING MEAN OUTS, POINT-IN-TIME — each comparable's mean outs over its OWN PRIOR 8 STARTS as of that game, so the grouping variable carries no lookahead** (the discipline the 8/22 T22 re-run already established after a season-long role label proved to be lookahead).

### 🔴 THE GRADIENT IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT — 88 STARTS AGAINST TEXAS, SPLIT BY THE STARTER'S DURABILITY GOING IN

| Starter's trailing mean outs | u15.5 outs hit rate |
|---|---|
| **under 14 — Johnson's own tier** | **5/9 = 55.6%** |
| 14–16 | 12/27 = 44.4% |

### ✅ 🆕 8/21 RE-VERIFICATION — A FULL-SEASON CONTROL, AND IT CAUGHT A LIVE FABRICATION

**All 12 of 8/20's graded lines were re-pulled from the flat `gameLog` endpoint and every one matched this table exactly.** Then a **stronger control than the one rule 10 specifies** was run: instead of checking that the season total moved by the game line, **every row of each pitcher's full game log was summed and compared to his independently-pulled season total.**

| | |
|---|---|
| 8/20 game lines matching this table | **12 / 12** ✅ |
| Full-season reconciliation (GS, outs, K) | **11 / 12 PASS** |
| Failures | **1 — Andrew Alvarez** |

🔴 **THE FAILURE WAS A FABRICATED SCALAR INSIDE A FLAT `gameLog` PAYLOAD — the route this project currently documents as the SAFE headless one.**

- Alvarez's log returned **`2026-05-24 | 1.3 IP`**. ⛔ **`1.3` IS NOT A VALID INNINGS-PITCHED VALUE.** The fraction is thirds: only `.0`, `.1` and `.2` exist.
- His log summed to **242 outs against a season total of 240 — short by exactly 2**, which pins the true value at **`1.1`**.
- ✅ **No graded line is affected.** That row is a **relief appearance** (`gamesStarted: 0`), it is **not 8/20**, and **his strikeout column reconciled exactly (74/74)** — no K value anywhere was corrupted.

➡️ 🔴 **THIS QUALIFIES A CLAIM THE DOCS CURRENTLY MAKE.** `claude/mlb-data-stack.md` says the flat game log is *"a shape a summarising fetch cannot merge."* **True — and insufficient. It cannot merge BLOCKS. It can still corrupt a SCALAR.** **The season control is not belt-and-braces; it is the only thing standing between this project and silent bad data.**

⚠️ **A second instance of the same family, same run:** the season-stats pull **reported its own row count as "1000" while enumerating 816.** The 816 values summed correctly to 3,838. 🔴 **Trust enumerated rows. Never trust a fetched summary's count of them.**

### 🔴 THE #1 PLAY LOST, AND IT LOST FOR A REASON THE MODEL CANNOT SEE

**Lambert o3.5 K at 86.1% — the highest-confidence play on the card — returned 3 K in 3.2 innings.** The Angels scored **18 runs** and he was gone after 79 pitches.

**The read was not wrong about the lineup.** LAA is the **2nd-easiest lineup in baseball to strike out (5.56 meanK, +0.47)** and that is exactly why he was #1. **They struck out plenty — against the relievers.**

➡️ 🔴 **THE STRIKEOUT MODEL HAS NO LENGTH TERM.** `E[K]` is built from his trailing K **per start** and the opponent's K **per start** — both of which silently embed an *average* outing length. **A strikeout count is bounded by how long he stays in the game, and nothing in the K model knows that.** The outs model exists and is never consulted when pricing a strikeout line.

⚠️ **DO NOT PATCH THIS OFF ONE START.** The opponent→outs channel was already measured and is **null (t=−0.34)** — on average a tough lineup does not shorten a start. **An 86.1% play loses 14% of the time and this is what that looks like.**

🆕 **OWED, PRE-REGISTERED as T1: add `E[outs]` as a term to the strikeout model at the monthly re-fit. Single specification, decided before looking.** **Log the result whichever way it falls.**

## Grading mechanics — READ BEFORE GRADING

Outs: `IP × 3`. `.1` = 1 out, `.2` = 2 outs. **5.2 IP = 17 outs.**
🆕 ⛔ **`.3` IS NOT A VALID FRACTION. See ledger rule 40 — a fetched `1.3 IP` on 8/21 was a fabricated scalar.**

### 🔴 W OR L. THERE IS NO VOID.
Pitcher props do not get voided. **A starter who exits after 1.0 IP is not an anomaly — he is an under that cashed.** *Push* exists only where a whole-number line lands exactly on the number, and **PrizePicks does post whole-number lines** (Roupp o4.0 and Bradish o6.0 on 8/20). **A line that never existed is a LOGGING ERROR** — out of the denominator, never a void.

### ✅ THE HEADLESS GRADING PATH — game log, one pitcher at a time, controlled

```
statsapi.mlb.com/api/v1/people/<id>/stats?stats=gameLog&season=<yr>&group=pitching&gameType=R
  &fields=stats,splits,date,stat,gamesStarted,inningsPitched,strikeOuts,numberOfPitches
```
🔴 **CONTROL IT. Two controls, and the second is stronger:**
```
(a) per-pitcher season totals, then check the season line moved by exactly the game line:
    /api/v1/people/<id>/stats?stats=season&season=<yr>&group=pitching&gameType=R
      &fields=stats,splits,stat,gamesStarted,inningsPitched,strikeOuts
(b) 🆕 BETTER — sum EVERY row of the game log and match it to that season total.
    A delta control only validates one row. A full-season sum validates all of them,
    and on 8/21 it is what caught the fabricated 1.3 IP.
```
⚠️ **`/api/v1/people?personIds=...&hydrate=stats(...)` returned a hard 403 twice through the fetch proxy** `[measured 8/21]` — the parenthesised `hydrate` appears to be the trigger. ✅ **The per-pitcher `stats=season` form above works. Use it.**

⚠️ **statsapi has returned a transient 403. RETRY ONCE.** 🔴 **Run the historical control before trusting an empty response** — `schedule?date=2025-08-19` returned `totalGames: 16` on 8/21 ✅.
🔴 **Never infer a scratch.**

⛔ **NEVER GRADE FROM THE BOXSCORE WITHOUT A BROWSER.** It carries `stats` and `seasonStats` side by side and a summarising fetch merges them — it reported a **75.0 IP / 69 K season line as a game line**, and **twice** claimed a two-starter game had no starters.

⛔ **ESPN is robots-blocked. B-Ref serves the previous day's slate and ignores the date query.** Neither is a same-night source.
